description: Discharge and load at T-01, T-03, T-04, T-06 and T-07 (about 60 container vessel calls a week): crane work queues, container moves, lashing, tally and completion messages to carriers
process_owner: Chief Operating Officer (with the Terminal General Managers)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: A vessel call has a fixed berth window of about 18 to 36 hours; a missed window delays the carrier service at the next ports. Container location, weight and hazardous cargo stowage data must be current to load safely. About 60% of revenue is earned on vessel work
manual_workaround: Paper bay plans and load lists from the carrier; crane work queues by radio from the superintendent; paper tally; reconcile in the TOS after recovery. Workable for about one shift at about 40% productivity; the automated yard at T-01 cannot run without the TOS and falls back to manual straddle carrier moves in 4 blocks
dependent_systems: SYS-01; SYS-03; SYS-05; SYS-06; SYS-07; SYS-08
dependent_third_parties: Ocean carriers; longshore hiring halls; crane and automation OEMs; Cloud provider A
dependent_people_or_facilities: Vessel planners; superintendents; longshore labor; 5 container terminals
quantified_impact_basis: About 60% of the $7.9 million a day of container vessel revenue deferred or lost while terminals work manually at about 40% productivity, plus about $1.1 million in overtime, vessel delay costs and berth window credits
single_points_of_failure: One TOS platform for 7 terminals (DEP-01); T-01 automated yard depends on the equipment control system

description: In-gate and out-gate at all 8 terminals (about 22,000 transactions a day): TWIC check, OCR of container, chassis and plate, appointment and customs hold check, interchange receipt
process_owner: Chief Operating Officer (with the Terminal General Managers)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Trucks queue on port and public roads within about 2 hours of a gate stop; port authorities charge congestion penalties. Releasing a container that is on a customs hold is a regulatory failure, so the gate stops rather than guesses. Gate transactions must not be lost
manual_workaround: Manual gate: clerks key container numbers from a printed release list, security officers check TWICs, paper interchange receipts; lanes cut to about one third; import deliveries only for containers confirmed released
dependent_systems: SYS-01; SYS-02; SYS-04; SYS-05; SYS-07; SYS-08; SYS-11
dependent_third_parties: Trucking companies; customs data exchange service; OCR vendor; port authorities
dependent_people_or_facilities: Gate clerks; security officers; 8 gate complexes
quantified_impact_basis: Gate, storage and appointment-related revenue of about $1.3 million a day, plus demurrage waivers, extended-gate overtime and port authority congestion charges of about $1.1 million a day
acquired_terminal_dependency: T-08 runs its own legacy gate system (BP-16)
single_points_of_failure: Customs data exchange service (DEP-08); SL-1 appointments (DEP-07)

description: Container inventory and location, RTG, straddle carrier and yard tractor dispatch through VMTs, the T-01 automated stacking crane yard, and reefer monitoring (about 3,800 plugs)
process_owner: Chief Operating Officer (with the Terminal General Managers)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Without current locations, containers are lost in the stacks and moves slow sharply. Reefers must be checked by hand every 4 hours when monitoring is down. A physical yard check rebuilds data but takes 1 to 2 shifts per terminal
manual_workaround: Printed yard inventory from the last export; radio dispatch; manual reefer checks every 4 hours; T-01 automated blocks switched to manual straddle carrier access in 4 of 15 blocks
dependent_third_parties: Automation vendor (T-01); VMT and wireless support
dependent_people_or_facilities: Yard clerks; equipment operators; reefer mechanics
quantified_impact_basis: Rehandles, lost productivity and overtime across 8 terminals, plus reefer claims exposure of about $300,000 a day if monitoring gaps cause spoilage

business_process: Maritime security, TWIC access control and hazardous cargo control
description: TWIC-based access to secure areas, CCTV, patrols, MARSEC level changes, and the dangerous cargo location list used by FSOs and emergency responders at 8 terminals
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Emergency responders must be able to find hazardous cargo at any time; FSP access control must continue at every MARSEC level (33 CFR Part 105). A failure could contribute to a transportation security incident (TSI)
manual_workaround: Security officers check TWICs visually and log entries by hand; printed dangerous cargo list at every shift change; CCTV recorders keep recording locally
dependent_third_parties: Port police and fire; Captains of the Port
quantified_impact_basis: Security overtime and manual TWIC checks; the dominant impact is regulatory and safety, not cost
acquired_terminal_dependency: T-08 PACS on its own server

business_process: Customs status and carrier EDI exchange
description: Receive release and hold status from the customs data exchange; exchange bay plans, load and discharge lists and container status with about 25 carriers; vessel schedules and gate status with 6 port community systems; rail interchange messages
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Holds and releases change through the day and drive every gate. Partners can resend the last 24 hours of messages, so a 1-hour RPO is enough, but an unreliable hold status stops import deliveries at all terminals
manual_workaround: Customs data exchange web portal for hold checks; carriers email bay plans and lists; port community system web screens
dependent_third_parties: Customs data exchange service; ocean carriers; port community systems (port authorities); rail partners
dependent_people_or_facilities: Integration operations team; planners; customer service
quantified_impact_basis: Import deliveries limited to containers confirmed by portal lookup (about 30% of normal), plus manual re-keying effort
acquired_terminal_dependency: T-08 has its own EDI links
single_points_of_failure: Single customs data exchange service provider (DEP-08)

description: Enterprise planning center: berth scheduling, stowage and crane split planning, yard allocation, and AI-001 scheduling optimization
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Plans are prepared 24 to 72 hours before arrival, so planning can pause for a day. Wrong stowage of heavy or hazardous containers is a safety issue, so plans made by hand need a second planner check
manual_workaround: Plan from carrier bay plans and spreadsheets; berth schedule shared by email and phone; AI-001 is not needed (planners can plan by hand)
dependent_people_or_facilities: About 60 planners at headquarters and terminals
quantified_impact_basis: Productivity loss from manual planning (about 8% more crane hours) for vessels planned during the outage

business_process: Crane, automation and equipment maintenance and OT engineering
description: Maintain 54 STS cranes, mobile harbor cranes, RTGs, straddle carriers, the T-01 automated stacking cranes and yard tractors; manage PLC and HMI programs and OEM diagnostics
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Cranes run on local controllers and can work without the TOS, but a crane with a corrupted PLC program cannot work at all. PLC programs change rarely, so the RPO is the last approved program version
manual_workaround: Run cranes in local mode with operators in the cab; isolate OT zones; reload controller programs from the company's program vault (T-01 to T-06) or from OEM copies (T-07, T-08)
dependent_people_or_facilities: About 2,250 maintenance and engineering staff; crane electrical houses
quantified_impact_basis: Each STS crane out of service removes about 1/6 of a berth's capacity; about $1.1 million a day if 10 cranes are down across terminals
acquired_terminal_dependency: T-08 PLC programs held only by the OEM

business_process: Ro-ro, breakbulk and project cargo operations
description: Vehicle processing, breakbulk and project cargo at T-02, T-05 and the breakbulk berth at T-08
process_owner: Chief Operating Officer (with the Terminal General Managers)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Vehicle and breakbulk work can run on paper manifests for about a day; customs holds still apply
manual_workaround: Paper manifests and vehicle lists; manual gate for vehicles
dependent_third_parties: Vehicle manufacturers and ro-ro carriers; customs data exchange
quantified_impact_basis: About $1.5 million a day of ro-ro and breakbulk revenue deferred, partly recoverable by overtime

description: Loading and unloading of intermodal trains at T-01 and T-04 (about 14 trains a week)
process_owner: Chief Operating Officer (with the Terminal General Managers)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Railroads can hold trains for about a day; missed cutoffs push boxes to trucks
manual_workaround: Paper rail lists from the railroads; manual load planning
dependent_people_or_facilities: Rail crews at T-01 and T-04
quantified_impact_basis: Missed train cutoffs and drayage to off-dock ramps

business_process: SL-1 Cargo Visibility and Appointment Platform
description: Container availability, holds and truck appointments for all 8 terminals; APIs for about 900 cargo owners, brokers and forwarders
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Every gate checks appointments in SL-1; without it gate volumes drop by about half. Subscription customers have availability commitments
manual_workaround: Appointments by phone and email on a shared list; availability lists emailed twice a day; gates accept walk-ins for confirmed releases
quantified_impact_basis: About $104,000 a day of SL-1 revenue plus service credits; the gate effect is counted in BP-02
acquired_terminal_dependency: T-08 uses SL-1 for appointments only

description: TOS and gate environments run on ETOP for 4 client terminals (C-01 to C-04)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Client terminals stop vessel and gate work when their TOS environment is down; their own BIAs set 4-hour RTOs. Clients rely on the company for systems they have delegated under Subpart F (101.615)
manual_workaround: Clients run their own manual procedures; the company provides printed exports on request
dependent_third_parties: Cloud provider A; TOS software vendor
dependent_people_or_facilities: TOS platform team; client success team
quantified_impact_basis: About $263,000 a day of SL-2 revenue plus service credits and liability caps under client agreements

description: Order labor from the hiring halls by the daily cutoffs, record hours, and feed payroll for guarantees
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Labor must be ordered before each hiring hall cutoff (usually the afternoon before the shift); a missed order idles a vessel. Hours must be recorded for collective bargaining agreement payments
manual_workaround: Phone and email orders to the hiring halls; paper time sheets
dependent_people_or_facilities: Labor relations and terminal labor coordinators
quantified_impact_basis: Idle vessel time and guaranteed pay for gangs ordered without work

description: Vessel and cargo handling invoices, demurrage and storage charges, SL-1 and SL-2 invoicing
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Charges can be rebuilt from TOS move history; cash impact grows after a week
manual_workaround: Queue invoices; rebuild charges from TOS history after recovery
quantified_impact_basis: About $12.8 million a day of invoicing is deferred, not lost; the impact is working capital and billing disputes

description: Monthly close, quarterly and annual SEC filings, SOX controls
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: A missed SEC filing deadline is severe; during the quarter-end close window the MTD drops to 48 hours
manual_workaround: Prior period data and manual journal entries
quantified_impact_basis: Overtime and advisor costs; the dominant impact is regulatory

description: Payroll for 12,000 employees, onboarding, terminations, training records
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Payroll runs biweekly; missing it has legal and retention impact
manual_workaround: Repeat the prior payroll through the payroll provider; paper timesheets
quantified_impact_basis: Rework and penalties if a payroll is missed

business_process: T-08 terminal operations on legacy systems
description: Vessel, yard, gate and billing at T-08 on the legacy TOS until migration (due 2027-06-30)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Same drivers as BP-01 to BP-03 at a smaller terminal. The legacy TOS backs up nightly to storage on the same network, so the real RPO is about 24 hours
manual_workaround: Paper procedures as at other terminals; manual gate
quantified_impact_basis: About $780,000 a day of T-08 revenue plus overtime
acquired_terminal_dependency: All of BP-16 depends on the T-08 legacy estate
single_points_of_failure: Legacy TOS on one on-premises server pair (DEP-21)
